entities.name: Komnenos
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Komnenos Dynasty (1081-1185 CE), one of the most capable Byzantine imperial houses, restored Byzantine military and political power after the catastrophic Battle of Manzikert (1071 CE) — where the Seljuk Turks had destroyed the Byzantine army, captured Emperor Romanos IV, and initiated the Turkification of Anatolia that would ultimately doom the empire — through a series of capable emperors (Alexios I, John II, Manuel I) who combined military reconquest, diplomatic sophistication, and cultural patronage in the Byzantine Empire's last period of genuine imperial power.

Alexios I Komnenos (r. 1081-1118 CE) is one of Byzantine history's most consequential rulers: seizing power in a military coup when the empire was near collapse (Norman invasion from the west, Seljuk advance from the east), he stabilized the empire through ruthless political skill, reformed the military using family members as commanders (a system of pronoia land grants), and in 1095 CE appealed to Pope Urban II for western mercenaries — a request that unexpectedly triggered the First Crusade (1096-1099 CE). His daughter Anna Komnene wrote the Alexiad, one of the greatest medieval historical narratives.

The Komnenian period (1081-1185) saw the Byzantine Empire as a major Mediterranean power, conducting the First Crusade's passage through Byzantine territory, fighting wars against Normans, Seljuks, and Serbs, and producing a remarkable cultural flourishing. Manuel I Komnenos (r. 1143-1180 CE) maintained Byzantine imperial prestige through brilliant diplomacy with western Crusader states, though his overextension contributed to the decline after his death. The Komnenian system of governing through family networks ultimately weakened the empire's institutional foundations.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Komnenos Dynasty — restoring Byzantine power after Manzikert, triggering the First Crusade through Alexios I's papal appeal, and producing the Alexiad, one of the medieval world's greatest historical narratives — is one of the most consequential Byzantine dynasties, whose actions helped shape the medieval Crusading era.
